analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md, so there is no code or enforcement change. The visible patch excerpt shows three edits. First, the 'Last updated' date bump. Second, a documentation addition near head lines 583-588 describing benchmark report schema 5 (prefillChunkTokens, maxBatchedTokensPerStep, and the requirement that a measured engine's geometry match the production build's prefill geometry). Third, a new row near head line 1755 in the daemon environment passthrough table. The row lists DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS as scheduler tunables read by EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (prefillChunkKey, stepTokenBudgetKey).

The supplied base units cover lines 831-1806, which are surrounding context. The changed hunks at head 583-588 and 1755 sit in regions outside the supplied base text, and the patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not verify the surrounding head lines for the new row.

Security relevance: the passthrough table documents which shell variables are copied into the LaunchAgent plist (LaunchAgent.swift passthroughEnvKeys/inferencePassthroughEnvKeys). The table carries only scheduler and performance tunables and no secrets, auth tokens or trust-affecting switches. Per the doc, any row in that list is forwarded from the invoking shell into the plist, so the new row implies that the two variables will be forwarded. Whether the code actually does this cannot be verified from the supplied evidence. The tunables are chunking and step-budget values that change throughput and memory behavior. They do not touch A-001 plaintext handling, attestation, App Attest authorization, or the SSD prefix-cache surfaces in T-041 (TTL, HMAC names, KEK, salt scoping).

The cache and prefix-cache doc text visible in the units (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE defaults, 30-minute TTL, SSD write budget) is unchanged context and consistent with the T-041 posture.

Remaining question for integration: whether the two newly documented env vars are actually added to the passthrough list in code, and whether any bounds apply to them. A pathological chunk or step value could affect availability or memory admission, but that would be a code-side concern, not evidenced here. No findings.
